runs.entry: Price **$66.41** a share (close 2026-10-16, `tools/run.py`'s live quote, aggregator, flagged). Shares **4,346,476** common, one class, no treasury shares (10-Q Q2 2026 cover as of 2026-07-31, `0001437749-26-027371`; the 2026 rights offering, 424B2 `0001437749-26-010183`, 713,362 shares at $59.00 completed 2026-04-27, inside the count; the Form 15-12G of 2026-05-13 deregisters the expired rights, not the common; the S-8 of 2026-09-23 registers plan shares, not issued); cap **$288.6M**. Sovereign **5.43%** (US Treasury 30-year par yield, 2026-10-16). Documents read: 10-K FY2025 (`0001437749-26-009844`), 10-Qs Q1 and Q2 2026, DEF 14A of 2026-04-30 (`0001437749-26-014017`), the 10-Ks FY2022 to FY2024, the Form 10 information statement of 2022 (carve-out 2020 and 2021, the named rivals), LGL Group 10-Ks FY2013, FY2016, FY2019 and FY2021 for the years before the separation of 2022-10-07, the 424B2s of 2025 and 2026, the 8-K/A of 2025-12-05 and the 8-Ks of 2025-12 to 2026-08. Cross-check: FY2025 operating cash $10,659K on the filed statement against 10.7 tagged. The brief's one stated departure: lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 1, 1A and 7 of the FY2025 10-K (ten lines, listed in Step 0). The FY2025 10-K names no rival; the 2022 Form 10 named divisions of larger filers (Vectron and Microsemi in Microchip, K&L Microwave in Dover) and Rakon, a foreign non-filer, so Frequency Electronics and Mercury Systems were read as a CONVENTION of the run. **Q1 IN**, narrowly: qualified frequency and spectrum control parts designed into defense, avionics and space programs, 2025 revenue $54.4M, aerospace and defense 65.2%. **Q2 TOO HARD (NATURE)**: one segment; a change for the better since 2023 (operating margin from about 9% to about 19%, gross margin 35.0% in 2021 to 46.2% in 2024 and 44.4% in 2025, backlog $29.4M in 2021 to $84.0M at mid-2026) that no year of falling volume has tested **[M2017-026]**, **[M2005-020]**, **[L1995-022]**, **[M2002-050]**, **[L1993-023]**, **[M2000-019]**, **[M2006-013]**. Against the castle: the filer's own "numerous domestic and international manufacturers" able to supply "comparable" custom products; no significant patents; two unnamed customers 50.9% of 2025 revenue; the same plants under LGL Group, then mostly telecom, fell from $46.7M of revenue (2010) to $20.7M (2015) with operating losses 2012 to 2015; Frequency Electronics with operating losses in 8 of 13 fiscal years FY2014 to FY2026, Mercury 8% to 12% margins through FY2021 and losses or break-even since FY2023. Against OUT: high returns on capital and a rising backlog, the castle not shown open on today's evidence. **Re-look condition**: the first fiscal year in which MPTI's revenue falls below the year before (or a year-end at which its backlog falls); Q2 put again on that year's margin and price behaviour. Q3 to Q12 not reached; no research pass, the cause being NATURE. Facts after the stop, recorded not judged: no debt, no goodwill; equity $16.8M (2021) to $118.7M (mid-2026), retained earnings $23.8M of the rise and paid-in capital $80.5M (the 2025 warrants $27.7M gross, the 2026 rights $42.1M gross, option exercises); cash $96.2M at 2026-06-30; plant 78% depreciated; the obsolete-stock reserve 13.1% to 14.6% of gross inventory. **Integrity facts recorded, not judged**: the CEO's statement leads with adjusted EBITDA excluding stock pay; the 2025 bonus kept out of 2025 expense and paid in stock in 2026 ($1.0M); the CEO's bonus 2% of the change in 7.5 times adjusted EBITDA plus cash, plus payments for completed acquisitions (8-K/A of 2025-12-05); two equity raises in two years with acquisitions and a strategic RF fund named as uses; GAMCO holds $94.4M of the cash and two GAMCO-affiliated directors are classed independent. Owner cash (operating cash less stock pay less capital spending, tax at the company's provision, before interest) 2021 to 2025 mean: **$3,076K** maintenance only (central), $2,358K after all spending; 2025 alone $6,596K; none computable before 2020. COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: value range **$35.35 to $42.43** a share (all-equity, maintenance, growth capped at the sovereign by the literal reading of (f)), net cash $97.0M, EV $191.6M; 1.6% to 2.6% at the price (7.0% on the 19.5% sales-growth reading), no case earns the floor, so Q7 would have closed OUT; fair **$30.99 all-equity** ($9.01 equity-only, which leaves out the $69.8M raised after the window; $39.69 and $18.04 on the sales-growth reading); not armed, the box being TOO HARD at Q2. Contamination declared by the analyst: one `Test Runs/` listing filtered for the company's names before the first fetch, returning nothing (unchecked in its self-audit), the ALFVY commit subjects and the memory index's queue-state lines; none used. Commits fcd290e7 (template), f8bda8fa (Step 0 to Q1), f7e516e9 (Q2), bf676515 (close). Position note filled at the fold: not held. Citations: the analyst's `scripts/check_citations.py` 45 ids, 52 fragments, PASS; the dispatcher's `dispatcher_cite_check.py` 45 ids, no missing id, no E-id, 52 fragments, five flags verified clean by hand (regex captures of the run's own prose beside M2008-033, M2005-020, M2005-017, L2014-015 and M2016-083, whose quoted fragments are in their rows): **no slip**. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator** (the analyst's framework notes): (1) Q7 (f)'s "never above the discount rate" read literally caps a 19.5% grower at the sovereign, read as the after-year-ten rule carries 19.5%; (2) Q7 (a) gives no fallback when the earlier cycle has no owner-cash figures (a predecessor's segment note only); (3) the equity-only figure when most of the cash was raised after the window; (4) section C when the business itself changed markets (telecom to defense); (5) rivals when the latest 10-K names none and the last named are divisions or non-filers; (6) Q1's third test and Q2's section C ask the same doubt, so two analysts could close the name at Q1 or at Q2. Could not get: owner cash before 2020, the two main customers and programs, unit volumes and share, the investor-day slides (images).
runs.narr: TOO HARD (NATURE) at Q2 (M-tron Industries, spun off by LGL Group 2022-10-07; frequency and spectrum control parts for defense, avionics and space). Q1 IN narrowly. A change for the better since 2023, margin from about 9% to about 19% and backlog $29.4M to $84.0M, that no year of falling volume has tested; against it the filer's own comparable rivals, no significant patents, two customers 50.9% of revenue, the same plants losing money as a telecom supplier 2012 to 2015, Frequency Electronics and Mercury ordinary or poor over the span; against OUT high returns and a rising backlog. Re-look at the first fiscal year revenue falls, or a year-end backlog falls. Integrity facts recorded, not judged: adjusted EBITDA featured, the 2025 bonus moved into 2026 stock pay, the CEO paid on 7.5 times adjusted EBITDA plus deal payments, two equity raises, GAMCO holding the cash. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: value $35.35 to $42.43 all-equity against $66.41, no case earning the floor, fair $30.99 all-equity, $9.01 equity-only, not armed. Framework gaps for the operator: Q7 (f)'s cap at the discount rate, no cycle base before a separation, equity-only with cash raised after the window, section C after a change of markets, Q1 against Q2 on the same doubt.
